title: Hitler's rise to power
issue: Why Hitler came to power in Germany by 1933

sources.provenance: A starting point for your answer
sources.text: In 1928 the Nazi Party was a small party on the edge of German politics. In January 1933 its leader, Adolf Hitler, became Chancellor of Germany. By 1939 most Germans supported or accepted his rule.

questions.question: 'The Great Depression was the main reason for Hitler's rise to power.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.

seeded.text: I agree. The Great Depression started in 1929 when the Wall Street Crash happened in America. Many Germans lost their jobs and became very poor. Hitler was also a good speaker and the Nazis used propaganda. The Weimar government was weak. So there were many reasons for Hitler's rise to power.

I agree to a large extent. The Great Depression made many Germans turn to Hitler. After the Wall Street Crash in 1929, American banks recalled their loans to Germany, and German businesses closed. By 1932 about six million Germans were unemployed. The Weimar government seemed unable to help, so desperate people looked for a party that promised strong action. Hitler promised work and bread. sources.text: Germany signed the Treaty of Versailles on 28 June 1919. Its terms took away territory, cut the armed forces and made Germany pay reparations.

questions.question: 'Gorbachev's policies were the main reason for the end of the Cold War.' How far do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer.

seeded.text: I agree. Gorbachev became the leader of the Soviet Union in 1985. He had two policies called glasnost and perestroika. He met President Reagan and they signed the INF Treaty in 1987. Reagan spent a lot of money on weapons and had a plan called the Strategic Defense Initiative. The Berlin Wall was opened in 1989. So the Cold War ended.

Gorbachev became leader of the Soviet Union in March 1985. He began glasnost, or openness, and perestroika, the restructuring of the economy. To carry out these reforms he needed to spend less on weapons, so he worked for better relations with the USA. He met President Reagan at Geneva in 1985 and at Reykjavik in 1986, and in December 1987 they signed the INF Treaty, which scrapped a whole class of nuclear missiles. He pulled the last Soviet troops out of Afghanistan in February 1989. He also let the countries of Eastern Europe choose their own governments, and the Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989. This shows that Gorbachev's choices slowed and then reversed the arms race and ended the division of Europe, the things that had kept the Cold War going. seeded.text: I agree. In 1989 there were many protests in Eastern Europe. In Poland there was a trade union called Solidarity led by Lech Walesa. In East Germany people marched in Leipzig and the Berlin Wall was opened on 9 November 1989. In Czechoslovakia there was the Velvet Revolution. Gorbachev was the leader of the Soviet Union at that time. So the communist governments fell.
